subject: DPA: incident notification & evidence handback - clarification
participants_external: james.han@finservco.com (James Han, Head of Security, FinServCo)
messages:
From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@finservco.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarification on DPA breach notification windows and cross-border evidence handback

Hi Irene,

Quick question as we review the Redwood DPA for FinServCo: section 7 on incident notifications currently references 'as soon as reasonably practicable' and a 'notification window' in a couple places. For our regulators we need explicit commitments on two points before we can finalize the SOW:

- The maximum elapsed time between detection and first customer notification once unauthorized access affecting FinServCo data is confirmed. Is Redwood willing to commit to a 72-hour maximum?
- Can you confirm the path for evidence handback (forensic snapshots, logs) when EU-hosted customer data is involved? Specifically: will Redwood provide evidence without cross-border transfer to the US by default, or will transfers occur and what safeguards (SCCs/DBT/contractual limits) apply?

Also: if a Redwood subprocessor needs to be engaged for forensic work, how will that be handled contractually and operationally? We have a standard NDA/limited-scope addendum and will share it if helpful.

I've attached the DPA excerpt we're referencing. Can we schedule a brief call tomorrow to align?

Thanks,
Alice Monroe
General Counsel
FinServCo

Attachment: Requested_DPA_snippet.pdf (pdf)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@finservco.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-18T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on DPA breach notification windows and cross-border evidence handback

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear note. Looping Ben (Security Ops) and Marissa (Customer Ops) so we can cover operational and legal angles.

Short answers up front:
- Notification window: Redwood's practice is to provide an initial customer notification as soon as we have confirmed unauthorized access affecting customer data and to follow with a substantive incident report within 72 hours of that confirmation. We can commit contractually to the 72-hour substantive window; initial provisional notifications (high-level heads-up) are typically sent earlier when we have credible indicators.
- Evidence handback / cross-border transfers: for EU customer data we will by default attempt to provide evidence and forensic artifacts in-region where feasible. If an export is required to conduct forensic work, transfers are governed by the DPA (SCCs or equivalent safeguards) and only performed with documented lawful basis and the minimal dataset necessary.
- Subprocessors / forensics vendors: Redwood treats forensic vendors as subprocessors. We maintain a subprocessors list and will either use a pre-approved vendor under our subprocessor arrangement or execute a targeted subprocessor agreement/BAA with FinServCo's addendum where needed. Operationally, we propose a joint triage and a scoped statement of work before any transfer or access.

Attachments: redwood_dpa_section7_response.docx; forensic-onboarding-checklist.txt

Next steps:
1) We can do a 30-minute call tomorrow (2025-09-19) between 09:00-11:00 PT — what time works for you?
2) If you can share the NDA addendum now, Ben will review for scope and Marissa will start a checklist for evidence packaging.

Level-set note on terminology: when we say 'confirmed' we mean after initial triage when Security + Product + Privacy agree there is credible evidence of unauthorized access to customer data (we'll outline the exact sign-off flow below). I want to be transparent that the timing of confirmation is a function of triage complexity.

Irene Choi
Head, Privacy & Legal
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_dpa_section7_response.docx (docx); forensic-onboarding-checklist.txt (text)

Irene, thanks — that helps. A couple of follow-ups before we lock the call:

- Please define 'confirmed' in concrete terms (what triggers the customer notification escalation vs a preliminary heads-up). We need a reproducible internal trigger for our audit record.
- For forensic snapshots: what is your expected turnaround for providing a snapshot of affected instances + associated logs? We're asking for a 5-business-day baseline for snapshots and a 72-hour baseline for log extracts, if possible.
- EU-only constraint: for any FinServCo EU-origin data we need evidence to remain within EU jurisdiction unless we explicitly agree otherwise. If Redwood needs to involve an external vendor in the US, we require (a) an SCC-based transfer or equivalent; (b) a minimal dataset approach; (c) our legal sign-off before transfer.

I am attaching our standard NDA addendum for limited-scope evidence handling. Can Ben join the call? Also proposing 2025-09-19 at 10:00 PT.

Thanks,
James Han
Head of Security
FinServCo

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-19T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on DPA breach notification windows and cross-border evidence handback

James / Alice — good to confirm timing. 10:00 PT tomorrow works for us; Ben and Marissa will join. Below are more concrete commitments we can put into contract language and operationalize during the call:

- \"Confirmed\" definition: internal triage triggers an escalation when Security detects indicators of unauthorized access to customer data and Security + Product + Privacy have completed an initial assessment to rule out false positives and identified at least one observable data access event attributable to a system/process change or compromised credential. We expect this triage & preliminary sign-off window to be 12-48 hours in most incidents; in complex supply-chain cases it can take longer but we will advise you.

- Notification cadence:
  * Provisional heads-up: within 24 hours if there are credible indicators but before full confirmation (we will label these as 'provisional').
  * Substantive customer notification: within 72 hours of confirmation (we will include scope, affected data classes, mitigations underway, and an outline of evidence available).

- Evidence delivery timelines:
  * Log extracts (agreed schema): within 72 hours after confirmation when technical feasibility allows.
  * Forensic snapshot (packaged, with chain-of-custody notes): target 5 business days for EU-scoped snapshots. This covers images and associated metadata; sensitive exports will be scoped to minimize PII.

- Cross-border and vendor controls:
  * Default preference is in-region handling for EU-origin data.
  * If Redwood requires a cross-border transfer (e.g., to Redwood engineering or a US-based subprocessor), we will: (1) document the minimal dataset; (2) rely on SCCs or equivalent safeguards; (3) obtain FinServCo sign-off prior to transfer unless emergency conditions prevent delay (in which case we will notify as soon as practicable and follow retroactive approval flows).
  * ForensicHub (forensics@forensichub.com) is an approved subprocessor we can stand up under our subprocessor terms; if you prefer ForensicHub under your NDA addendum we can execute a narrow subprocessor addendum.

- Next steps for the call (agenda):
  1) Align on 'confirmed' trigger language for the DPA redline.
  2) Agree evidence delivery artifacts and formats (log schema + container formats).
  3) Decide on vendor engagement path and sign-off flow for any cross-border transfers.
  4) DocuSign execution of limited scope evidence transfer if needed.

I will bring a draft DPA redline for section 7 and a flow diagram illustrating in-region evidence packaging (attached: evidence-transfer-flow.png). For the DocuSign route, here is a pre-populated link for limited-scope evidence transfer approval: https://docusign.com/rs/ABCD1234

Marissa will follow up with a short checklist we can use to capture the required artefacts during triage.

Best,
Irene
Head, Privacy & Legal
Redwood Inference
